@matthiasott @zastrow

This poll got a lot of responses (and helpful replies)!

I wasn’t all that interested in preferences 😅. I really wanted to learn about the folks that selected the first two options.

A few lessons:

1. Supporting both modes is an accessibility priority—some folks need light, some dark.
2. Which mode folks need can be dependent on their surroundings (not just time of day).
3. Untested poor color contrast is a big problem!
4. UI toggles are used by folks as a workaround for color contrast issues.
@zachleat I think from the responses there is a question about what "poor" colour contrast is, though. Several people struggled when the contrast was too high, as well as too low.

@sarajw This is the trouble with getting into the whole contrast area of thought: there is no "one good design". For some people, whatever you do it's too high contrast, too low contrast, too much glare, etc etc. Heck even the color contrast algo in the a11y criteria is wonky compared with how most people see colours. @zachleat

@sarajw (I also happen to think a lot of the preferences depends on the literal physical context of where people are sitting looking at screens, which in turn depends on the time of day they do it, which direction the room and windows are facing, etc. It's all massively subjective.) @zachleat
